title: Process Equivalence and Canonical Continuation Forms
purpose: Define when two continuation expressions are process-equivalent and introduce canonical forms for continuation algebra.

canonical_claims.statement: Symbolic equality is not sufficient for RT Calculus equivalence.
Process equivalence compares lawful continuation behavior.
Two continuation expressions may differ syntactically while being process-equivalent.
Every well-formed continuation expression should reduce toward a canonical continuation form when admissibility holds.
Canonical forms support auditability, comparison, and eventual execution.

formal_objects.name: Process Equivalence
formal_objects.definition: A binary process-equivalence relation on continuation expressions that holds when they produce the same admissible continuation behavior under the same governing conditions; it is not mere symbolic equality.

formal_objects.name: Canonical Continuation Form
formal_objects.definition: The canonical representative of a continuation expression when admissibility holds; it supports auditability and comparison without specifying the reduction algorithm.

laws.name: Process Equivalence
laws.formal: C1 ≡P C2 iff Behavior(C1) = Behavior(C2) under shared admissibility, residue, orientation, and context constraints
laws.meaning: Two continuations are process-equivalent only when they induce the same lawful continuation behavior under the same governing conditions.

laws.name: Canonical Form
laws.meaning: A canonical continuation form names the normalized representative of a continuation expression when admissibility holds.

laws.name: Equivalence by Normal Form
laws.meaning: Matching canonical continuation forms imply process equivalence.

laws.name: Non-Converse Warning
laws.formal: C1 ≡P C2 does not necessarily imply identical syntax
laws.meaning: Process equivalence compares lawful behavior and does not collapse into surface equality.

validation_requirements: Process equivalence registered in the formal object registry.
Canonical continuation form registered in the formal object registry.
Do not collapse process equivalence into symbolic equality.
